html:
The Nunggubuyu are an Aboriginal Australian people of the southeast coast of Arnhem Land in the Northern Territory, around the Rose River and the community of Numbulwar.

Their language, Wubuy, belongs to the non Pama-Nyungan languages of the north. Their neighbours were the Ngandi inland, the Yolngu to the north and the Anindilyakwa of Groote Eylandt across the water. Makassan trepang boats from Sulawesi, part of the Makassan trepang trade, visited this coast for generations. The Church Missionary Society founded the Numbulwar mission in the 1950s.
sum: The Nunggubuyu are an Aboriginal Australian people of the southeast coast of Arnhem Land in the Northern Territory, around the Rose River and the community of Numbulwar.
